messages:
Maya: Heads-up — p95/p99 latency jumped on canary after the tokenizer+kernel bundle (v8.0) went to 10% at ~18:20 UTC. Observability shows kernel selector flips, and KV cache hit rate dropped. Graphs: step increase around 18:22. @oncall please triage.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout to 10% completed at 18:20:03, snapshot id=canary-2026-03-18-1820. Auto-rollback threshold NOT hit (yet).

Liam: I pulled the profiler traces from the canary hosts. Quick summary: kernel selection moved from 'fused-attn' -> 'attn-raw' for a subset of seq-len patterns. Batcher started coalescing heterogeneous seq-lens after token counts changed with the new tokenizer. p99 per-token went from ~22ms -> ~46ms for affected requests.

Rowan: KV cache metrics: baseline hit_rate ~97%, canary hosts reporting ~65% hit_rate, miss spike at 18:21:30. Looks like tokenization boundaries changed so cached prefixes don't match (prefix hashes differ).

Maya: Copy. Any obvious cause why tokenization changes would flip kernel selection?

Liam: Yes — the selector uses observed seq-length distribution + a padding heuristic to pick kernels and batching bins. With tokenizer v8 we now emit more subtokens for long words (more splitting), which shifts the effective sequence histogram. The batcher groups based on reported token counts and then we pad to max in each micro-batch; that increases effective compute and triggers a different kernel that handles larger padded workloads but has worse per-token latency for small live cases.

Hema: Can we force a kernel override on canary nodes while we investigate? We should avoid rolling back everything immediately if an override buys time.

Liam: Pushing kernel_override=fused-attn to canary host-group now. Command: `deployctl override-kernel --group canary --kernel fused-attn`

Maya: Log snippet from canary host (18:20-18:25):
```
kernel_choice: attn-raw -> p99=46.2ms
kvcache: hits=6521 misses=3521 hit_rate=65.3%
batcher: avg_batch_pad=112 tokens increased from 24 -> 136
```

Rowan: After the override, I see p99 drop back toward baseline within two batches. kvcache hit_rate is climbing back up to ~88% as batcher bins stabilize.

perf-bot: Alert: latency_p99.canary decreased 44% after kernel_override applied. Alert resolved at 18:24:07.

Maya: Good — temporary mitigation worked. We should pause the tokenizer v8 rollout. I'm going to create a rollback ticket and mark the canary as stable->reverted.

Liam: Filed INFR-1234 to revert tokenizer v8 for the next canary wave and to add a gating test. Action items:
- add a unit/integration test that compares seq-len histogram delta between tokenizers (fail if delta > threshold)
- add a guard in the kernel selector to avoid flipping kernels on <N% changes in seq distribution in a rolling window
- add KV cache prefix normalization or tokenization-version tag so caches don't collide when tokenizer changes

Hema: Also propose adding a small canary traffic experiment that simulates chat-history-prefixed requests (long contexts) since that's where we saw the worst effect.

Rowan: Agreed. I'll draft the repro and a short regression test harness.

Maya: TL;DR: cause = tokenizer v8 changed subtokenization -> seq-len distribution shift -> batcher padding up -> kernel selector switched to different kernel -> p99 spike + KV cache mismatch. Mitigation = kernel override + pause rollout. Follow-ups assigned in INFR-1234.

Liam: Note for postmortem: we should surface "tokenizer version" in tracing so we can correlate tokenization artifacts with perf traces automatically.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Marking this thread resolved for now, keeping the ticket open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

oncall: Acknowledged, will monitor canary hosts for 60m and escalate if anything re-escalates.
